dish.title: Filipino Fish Sinigang with Tamarind Broth
dish.description: A bright, sour tamarind broth simmered with tomato, onion, daikon, and green beans, then finished by gently poaching chunks of red snapper and wilting bok choy. Served with steamed jasmine rice.

recipe_version.title: Filipino Fish Sinigang with Tamarind Broth
recipe_version.description: A bright, sour tamarind broth simmered with tomato, onion, daikon, and green beans, then finished by gently poaching chunks of red snapper and wilting bok choy. Served with steamed jasmine rice.

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Quarter the tomatoes, cut the onion into wedges, and slice the ginger. Peel and slice the daikon; trim and cut the green beans; halve the bok choy. Cut the snapper into 2-inch pieces, sprinkle with the salt, and refrigerate. In a small bowl stir the tamarind paste into 1/2 cup hot water until smooth. Rinse the rice.

steps.title: Start the broth
steps.body: Put 8 cups water, the tomatoes, onion, and ginger in a 6-quart pot. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the vegetables
steps.body: Uncover, reduce to medium-low, and simmer 10 minutes, until the tomatoes slump. Add the daikon and simmer 8 minutes more. Meanwhile combine the rice and 2 1/4 cups water in a 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, cook on low 15 minutes, and rest covered off the heat; this runs inside the broth simmer and step 4 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Sour and season
steps.body: Strain the tamarind mixture (the paste loosened in its 1/2 cup water) into the pot through a fine-mesh strainer, pressing on the solids. Add the fish sauce, the whole serranos, and the green beans; simmer 4 minutes.

steps.title: Poach the fish and serve
steps.body: Lower the heat so the broth barely bubbles. Slip in the snapper and the bok choy and poach 5 to 6 minutes, without stirring, until the fish is opaque, just flaking, and 145 F. Taste for sourness and salt. Ladle into deep bowls and serve the rice alongside.

coverage_contribution: Filipino 1 to 2 (adobo is chicken). First sour broth and first fish soup in the catalog. Red snapper is a new species. HH001 soup.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with vietnamese-chicken-pho and miso-mushroom-ramen: no noodles, no spiced or miso stock; a sour tamarind broth with fish. Compared with brazilian-fish-moqueca: clear broth, no coconut, no peppers. Compared with vietnamese-turmeric-dill-fish: poached in broth, not seared with turmeric. Compared with korean-soft-tofu-stew: no tofu, no gochugaru.
not_duplicate_of: Not pork sinigang (wave-14 already carries several pork mains; this one is HH001 fish).
